- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and forecasts too high — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.27 or higher) and price is falling, model may underestimate support — raise forecast slightly to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply a +0.5–1.5% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.16), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.  
- If true outcome is consistently lower than forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), model may be overconfident — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 7 days if sentiment remains flat or mildly negative.
